Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) Tells his son, "We are the leaders to be followed"

Hadhrat Mus'ab bin Sa'd reports that whenever his father (Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA)) led the salaah (in congregation), he would make it brief together with performing the Ruku and Sajdah properly. However, when performing salaah at home (by himself), he would prolong the Ruku, the Sajdah and the salaah. He would then say, "Dear son! We (the Sahabah (RA)) are the leaders to be followed." [^2]
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Follow and do not introduce" and his Statement about Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA)

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "Follow and do not introduce (new ways) because everything has been done for you (Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) have already blazed the trail)." [^3]
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also said, "An integral part of the Sunnah is to love Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA) and to acknowledge their worth." [^4]
Hadhrat Ali (RA) Forbids People from Following Living People

Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Be careful not to emulate people because while a man can be doing the deeds of the people of Jannah, he can change according to the knowledge of Allaah and then start doing the actions of the people of Jahannam. When he then dies, he becomes an inmate of Jahannam. It may also happen that while a man can be doing the actions of the people of Jahannam, he can change according to the knowledge of Allaah and then start doing the deeds of the people of Jannah. When he then dies, he becomes a worthy dweller of Jannah. However, if it is absolutely necessary for you to follow someone, let it be those who have died (as practising Mu'mineen) and not those who are alive." [^5]
